title: Normalized derived tensor and transposition under ringed forgetting
statement:
Let $(C,R)$ and $(C',R')$ be small ringed sites with commutative ring sheaves, in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Put $\mathcal B=\operatorname{Mod}(R)$ and $\mathcal A=\operatorname{Mod}(R')$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and use unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $U:\mathcal B\to\mathcal A$ be exact additive, preserving small products and coproducts, with coherent underlying-module identifications for sheaf tensor, tensor unit and sheaf internal Hom, preserving their symmetry and evaluation. Assume termwise $U$ preserves K-injective complexes and K-flat complexes with flat terms [def-pur-kinjective-complex, def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. Write $F=D(U)$. Use total K-flat derived tensors and their signed symmetric monoidal structures [lem-sf-ringed-derived-closed-symmetric-monoidal] and derived internal Homs $H_{\mathcal B},H_{\mathcal A}$ [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. On both sites fix precisely the evaluation-normalized adjunction of [lem-sf-ringed-derived-tensor-hom-adjunction, def-coef-ringed-tensor-hom-model]. Let $\chi_{K,L}:FH_{\mathcal B}(K,L)\simeq H_{\mathcal A}(FK,FL)$ be the natural comparison of [lem-sf-ringed-forget-two-injective-hom] (whose hypotheses hold here), given on K-injective representatives by the product [def-pur-hom-complex] of the specified underived sheaf-Hom [def-pur-sheaf-hom] identifications.

There is a natural isomorphism $\mu_{K,L}:F(K\otimes^{\mathbf L}L)\simeq FK\otimes^{\mathbf L}FL$, whose representative on K-flat flat-term complexes $P,Q$ is $U\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes_RQ)\simeq\operatorname{Tot}(UP\otimes_{R'}UQ)$, induced on every summand by the underived tensor identification. Both differentials on bidegree $(p,q)$ are $d_P\otimes1+(-1)^p1\otimes d_Q$. The comparison extends uniquely from these representatives to all derived objects and morphisms; it preserves the unit, associativity, and the symmetry $x\otimes y\mapsto(-1)^{pq}y\otimes x$.

These specified $\mu$ and $\chi$ commute with the specified derived adjunctions: for every $a:M\to H_{\mathcal B}(K,L)$, uncurrying $\chi_{K,L}\circ F(a)$ gives $F(\operatorname{uncurry}(a))\circ\mu_{M,K}^{-1}$. On simultaneous K-flat source models and a K-injective target this equation uses exactly the chain map $x\otimes y\mapsto\phi(x)(y)$ followed by the inverse localized target augmentation; it is independent of all representative choices. In particular $\operatorname{ev}_{FK,FL}\circ(\chi_{K,L}\otimes1)\circ\mu_{H_{\mathcal B}(K,L),K}=F(\operatorname{ev}_{K,L})$.

For any $W\in D(\mathcal B)$ let $D_WK=H_{\mathcal B}(K,W)$ and define $\delta_K^W:K\to D_WD_WK$ to be the transpose, for this same adjunction, of evaluation after symmetry. These maps are natural in $K$, and under the iterated $\chi$ identifications $F\delta_K^W$ is exactly $\delta_{FK}^{FW}$. Neither double-dual map is asserted to be invertible.

proof.text: Apply the tensor-only descent theorem to obtain t and uniqueness of its derived transformation.

The normalized uncurrying theorem gives hu for the fixed two-injective comparison and t.derive. At the identity arrow, adjunction uncurrying is evaluation; multiply by the tensor comparison and cancel its inverse to obtain evaluation preservation.

For any closed symmetric monoidal category, uncurry both proposed naturality composites for delta. Naturality of evaluation in its contravariant parameter and naturality of the braiding make them equal. Injectivity of the adjunction gives delta naturality on each site.

Uncurry the iterated Hom comparison applied to F delta. Contravariant adjunction naturality introduces tensor(1,chi inverse). The uncurry equation replaces the remaining transpose. Tensor symmetry coherence and the evaluation equation cancel mu and chi with their inverses. Braiding naturality leaves symmetric evaluation on the target; adjunction injectivity gives delta_forget. Assemble the original Comparison fields and reuse the tensor transformation uniqueness proof.
